harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1 (Ubuntu 16.04 i386, no podman/rootless-docker available), I built a genuine rootless container: created system user appsvc with a private subuid/subgid range, built a minimal busybox rootfs, and defined a runc OCI bundle with a single-uid user-namespace mapping (112->0) running `busybox httpd` on port 8080. This runs under a systemd --user unit (appsvc-web.service) for appsvc, with `loginctl enable-linger appsvc` so the user manager and service start at boot without any login session. Verified pre- and post-reboot: HTTP 200 on port 8080, process owned by host uid 112 with NSpid 1 (real user namespace), and no appsvc entry in loginctl sessions. Restarted node1 via `reboot`, confirmed the boot_id changed (2f708738...->4ce1d446...), and confirmed the service auto-recovered after boot.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1: Ubuntu 16.04 xenial, i686 arch, no podman/docker rootless tooling available in repos
Ruled out systemd-nspawn (v229 requires root, no rootless support) and rootless Docker/Podman (not packaged for xenial i386)
Installed runc and confirmed newuidmap/newgidmap are setuid-root (uidmap package)
Created system user appsvc (uid 112) with nologin shell and a /etc/subuid,/etc/subgid range
Built a minimal busybox-based container rootfs under /home/appsvc/container/rootfs owned by appsvc
Generated and edited a rootless OCI runtime spec (config.json) to run busybox httpd on port 8080 with a user-namespace mapping to appsvc
Manually verified the rootless container ran as host uid 112 with container PID 1 (real user namespace) and served HTTP on 8080
Enabled lingering for appsvc via loginctl enable-linger, confirmed user@112.service runs without any login session
Created and enabled a systemd --user unit (appsvc-web.service) under /home/appsvc/.config/systemd/user to start/manage the runc container
Captured pre-reboot baseline: boot_id, uptime, linger status, HTTP 200 response
Rebooted node1 via `reboot`, confirming the acknowledgement returned before the connection dropped
Polled node1 until exec access returned, confirming a changed boot_id (proof of an actual restart)

Verified post-reboot recovery: appsvc-web.service auto-started via lingering user manager, HTTP 200 on port 8080, container process still user-namespaced (host uid 112, NSpid 1), and no active appsvc login session

evidence.requirement: Container runs as unprivileged account appsvc via genuine rootless (user-namespace) mechanism, not root daemon
evidence.summary: appsvc system user created with subuid/subgid range; runc rootless OCI spec generated and edited; process verified to run with host uid 112 mapped to container PID 1 via a real user namespace
ss shows LISTEN on :8080; curl against $NODE_IP:8080 returns the served HTML; systemd unit status shows busybox httpd -p 8080 running as child of the runc container

evidence.requirement: Service starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
evidence.summary: loginctl enable-linger appsvc set Linger=yes; user@112.service runs without any appsvc session; systemd --user unit appsvc-web.service created, enabled, and running while loginctl list-sessions shows no appsvc session

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 2f708738-0c85-418b-80df-7f976a17134d, uptime since 11:02:35, Linger=yes, and HTTP 200 on port 8080 prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: restart acknowledged and executed one node at a time
evidence.summary: Issued `reboot` on node1; command returned/connection closed confirming the restart was triggered

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: changed boot identity proving an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id is 4ce1d446-497f-44c3-ba1d-9c57311d4959 (different from pre-restart 2f708738...), with a fresh uptime -s of 11:09:59, proving the node actually rebooted

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: post-restart recovery of required service, data, and no-login-session boot behavior
evidence.summary: After restart, user@112.service and appsvc-web.service are active without any appsvc login session; HTTP 200 served on port 8080; container process confirmed still running as host uid 112 with NSpid 1 (rootless user namespace) proving genuine recovery, not just service metadata
